# nonRange

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a range.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonRange() — Checks whether a value is **not** a range. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/sheet</code> · Since: 1.3.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonRange<T>(value: T | GoogleAppsScript.Spreadsheet.Range): value is T;
```

`nonRange(value)` is the same test as `!isRange(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard reads the tag the object reports for itself: `value.toString() === "Range"`. A plain object that reports the same tag passes too, which in practice means a test double.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type                                      | Description         |
| :-------- | :---------------------------------------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| GoogleAppsScript.Spreadsheet.Range` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a range; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
const range = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveRange();

nonRange({}); // => true
nonRange(null); // => true
nonRange(range); // => false
```
